title: Timer Struct
story: You're building a cooking app and need a countdown timer. It starts at 1 hour, 30 minutes, 45 seconds. You want to add seconds, convert the whole thing to total seconds, and tick the timer down. Mutating methods make this feel like a real ticking clock.
why: A struct with mutating methods models stateful objects like timers, counters, and game clocks.
analogy: A Timer is like a digital kitchen clock. total_seconds is the raw internal counter. add_seconds is you pressing the "+30s" button. The display method is the clock face — it reads the internal time in a human-friendly format.
try_it: Add a `reset` method that sets hours/minutes/seconds to 0. Add a `Timer.tick(self)` method that adds 1 second (call add_seconds(1)). Create a countdown timer starting at 10 minutes and tick it 5 times. Add overflow: create a timer at 23h 59m 59s and tick it once.
tips: Overflow into hours and minutes: `total / 3600` for hours, `(total % 3600) / 60` for minutes
`self.total_seconds()` inside `add_seconds` reuses the same conversion logic — no duplication
Use `var` for the timer so `add_seconds` can mutate its fields
common_mistakes: Trying to add seconds without converting to total first — adding directly to the `seconds` field won't handle overflow into minutes
Forgetting to multiply hours by 3600 and minutes by 60 in `total_seconds`
